newsitem.title: JAPAN: Problem loans at Hanwa Bank total 190 bln yen - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Problem loans at Hanwa Bank total 190 bln yen - MOF.

text.p: Problem loans held at failed Hanwa Bank Ltd total 190 billion yen, a senior official at the Ministry of Finance told reporters on Thursday.
He said the capital of Hanwa as of the end of September was 20.3 billion yen.

The official said the ministry made the decision to halt most of Hanwa's operations because the bank would not have been able to boost its capital before its announcement of first-half earnings this week.
Kimio Yamaguchi, director-general of MOF's banking bureau, told reporters that of the 190 billion in problem loans, 40 billion yen would be unrecoverable.
If Hanwa had been able to recover its problem loans quickly, MOF would not have decided to wind it up, he said.

Even if banks in general held an excess of liabilities over assets, the ministry would not take the same action as it had with Hanwa Bank if those banks were able to recover from such a financial state within a short time, he added.
